src: Arienzo BIRTH registers — the annual tavole. ANTENATI an_ua14428 (1831, 100 images) and an_ua14433 (1836, 128 images), the last three openings of each.
what: Whether the Arienzo birth volumes of the 1830s carry a usable alphabetical tavola, which is the cheap way to find one child in a year of 130 births
got:
**THEY DO NOT, AND THE TWO YEARS FAIL IN DIFFERENT WAYS.**

**1831 has no tavola at all.** The volume ends with its last acts — 244, 245 and 246, all late December — then two blank leaves and the Procuratore del Re's certificate. There is no index page anywhere at the back.

**1836 has a tavola and it was never filled in.** Image 127 right carries the printed heading «*Tavola alfabetica annuale de' Nati per l'anno milleottocento*» over its ruled columns — **Cognomi e Nomi de' Nati · Cognomi e Nomi de' Genitori · Giorno della Nascita** — and every cell is empty.

**So the shortcut this archive has used for 1824, 1825 and 1828 is not available in the 1830s.** Finding one child in these years means sweeping the register itself at the declarant band, a hundred to a hundred and fifty images a year. **That is a cost to plan for, not a gap to be surprised by** — and a blank tavola is easy to record as «not read» when it is in fact empty.

src: Arienzo deaths register, 1836 — ANTENATI an_ua14338, 51 images
what: All 51 images swept at the band carrying the dead person's NAME, AGE and TRADE — read for RELIGIOUS, not only for Falco. **1836 is the one year between 1824 and 1843 with no index in the series**, so the register is the only way in.
got:
**DON GIUSEPPE CIOFFI IS NOT HERE, and that closes the last gap.** The year buries **eight religious**: **Don Gennaro Esposito**, *sacerdote*, ninety; **Don Alessandro Bruno**, *sacerdote*, twenty-seven; **Don Francesco de Gentij**, *sacerdote*, forty-six; a **Diglio** *sacerdote*; **Don Antonio Cimmino**, ***seminarista***, twenty-four; **Suor Fedele Ruggiero**, sixty-three; **Donna Carlotta Rauti**, seventy-three; and **Donna Raffaela de' Falco**, *monaca*, sixty-seven. **None is a Giuseppe of about fifty-six.**

**And it gave a brother to generation four's mother-in-law.** Act 50, 11 August 1836: «*è morto nella propria casa **PASQUALE DI GUIDA d'anni CINQUANTASETTE** … di professione **SENSALE** … **figlio di GIUSEPPE DI GUIDA** … **e di MADDALENA RIVETTA Defunta***» — the same two parents as **ANTONIA DI GUIDA**. Declared by **CLEMENTE DI GUIDA**, thirty-three, *sensale*, and **CARLANTONIO MORGILLO**, fifty, *contadino* of **strada Camellara**.

**Two of this archive's own contested readings were confirmed in passing**, both at 3,200 pixels: **Margarita Falco**'s husband is **DOMENICO COSPI** (the surname is in the left margin, not on the line) and her mother **MARIANGELA IULIUCCIO**.

src: Arienzo civil MARRIAGES 1815 — ANTENATI an_ua14219, 30 images
what: All twenty-five acts, read for FALCO as spouse, parent or witness. Images 17–30 — acts 16 to 25 — had never been opened; they were read at 3,200 pixels on 20 September 2026.
got:
**One Falco in the year, and he is not claimed.** Act 8 is **LUIGI FALCO, eighteen, *sapunaro*** — soap-maker — of the Comune de' Sei Casali, that is **San Felice a Cancello**, son of **SEBASTIANO FALCO and COLOMBA MONTEFUSCO**. **Acts 16 to 25 hold no Falco at all**: Loffredo, Morgillo, Verdicchio, Grossi, Carfora, Morgillo, Ferriello, Arrigale, Marletta, Buono.

**Two things worth having came out of the unread half.** Act 20 is a gentry marriage — **Signor PASQUALE CARFORA, *medico cerusico*** of Santa Maria a Vico — naming his parents **PAOLO CARFORA** and **ANNA SABATELLI** with their deaths recited, **6 November 1782** and **22 January 1789**. And act 21 names **ELISABETTA COSSI**, daughter of the late **MARINO COSSI** — a documented **COSSI** household, which is the control this archive needed while correcting *Cossi* to *Cioffi* on strada Camellara.

**The volume's own arithmetic was wrong here until today**: image *N* right holds act *N−1*, so images 17–30 are **ten** acts and not twelve, and images **24 and 25 are duplicate photographs** of openings already filmed.

src: Arienzo deaths register, 1816 — ANTENATI an_ua14318, 47 images
what: Every act, read for FALCO as deceased, parent, spouse or declarant
got:
No Falco died. But act 76 names TWO Falco declarants of strada Camellara — Gioacchino Falco, 36, and Giuseppe Falco, 32 — described as «parenti del defunto», and the dead man, Crescenzo Rivetti, is «marito di Angela Falco».

A Falco head this archive had never met, and a Falco marriage it did not have. No Raffaele Falco burial here — he turned up in the next volume, on 28 October 1817. IMAGES 3-39 WERE RE-READ IN 2026 and are now rostered act by act: that second pass found the CIOFFI already on strada Camellara in 1816, and joined the head of the Monticello Morgillo house to his own parents, Simone Morgillo and Gaetana Laudato.

src: Arienzo deaths register, 1817 — ANTENATI an_ua14319, 89 images
what: Every act, read for FALCO as deceased, parent, spouse or declarant
got:
THE BURIAL OF THE FIRST RAFFAELE FALCO, 28 October — son of Vincenzo and Andreana, aged about eighteen months, declared by Giuseppe Falco of strada Camellara as a «parente». Also Maria Falco, 24 July, daughter of a Giuseppe Falco and Rosa Sossi neither of them known before; and, in the 1818 acts bound at the back, Angela Majone, daughter of a second Maria Falco.

The volume that answered the archive's largest open question. Nearly twice the size of 1816 because 1817 was the famine year after Tambora — whole households die within days of each other.

But Giuseppe Falco of strada Camellara declares again on 8 May — thirty-six, contadino — four weeks before his own daughter's birth act gives exactly the same age, trade and street, which proves the five sightings are one man. Also a SECOND Carlantonio Morgillo, older and already dead; an Orazio Morgillo of the right age to be Angela Rosa's father; and Don Giuseppe Rivetti, a priest.

Its first eleven images are a second original of acts the 1817 volume already held — two clerks who disagree in detail, which caught a misreading in this archive's own notes.

src: Arienzo deaths register, 1819 — ANTENATI an_ua14321, 37 images

DOMENICO FALCO and ROSARIA FALCO, both on 15 March, eleven hours apart — two children of Giuseppe Falco and Gelsomina Vigliotta dead in one day. And ANGELANDREA RIVETTI, daughter of the late Crescenzo Rivetti and ANGELA FALCO: the only other record anywhere that names Angela.

Also Suor Maria Maddalena Rivetti, a nun, daughter of a Don Giuseppe Rivetti — the fourth gentry Rivetti, in a town where the same surname is also full of day-labourers.

src: Arienzo deaths register, 1820 — ANTENATI an_ua14322, 43 images
what: Every act, read for FALCO as deceased, parent, spouse or declarant
got:
ANNA FALCO, 23 August, aged twenty-five — «moglie di Arcangelo Crisci … FIGLIA DI PASQUALE FALCO … E DI CHIARA RIVETTI». A daughter of the direct line's generation two that this archive did not have, and a sister of Vincenzo. Also her two-day-old son Fortunato Crisci, in January.

Both her parents are named without «fu», so Pasquale Falco and Chiara Rivetti were alive on strada Camellara in August 1820 — the only civil sighting of him between his marriage and his death. From 1820 the printed form also gives the deceased's age, both parents, and each declarant's relationship.

src: Arienzo deaths register, 1821 — ANTENATI an_ua14323, 37 images

But CARMINE RIVETTI, 53, a contadino, «figlio di NICOLA RIVETTI Defunto, di professione CONTADINO, e di ANNA DI RUGGIO Defunta» — a rival and better-fitting candidate for Chiara Rivetti's parents than the gentry couple of 1816.

Also a third Carlantonio Morgillo, checked and cleared; and a death in the Regie Prigioni of Arienzo, declared by the gaol's keeper — this archive did not know the town had a prison.

src: Arienzo deaths register, 1822 — ANTENATI an_ua14324, 44 images
what: Every act, read for FALCO as deceased, parent, spouse or declarant
got:
ANGELA FALCO, 17 October, aged fifty-one — «vedova di CRESCENZO RIVETTI … FIGLIA DI MATTEO FALCO Defunto … E DI FRANCESCA CRISCI Defunta». A daughter of the founding couple, and a sister of Pasquale.

The earliest of three separate children's death acts to name Matteo and Francesca. It also explains why Gioacchino Falco and Giuseppe Falco declared her husband's death in 1816 as «parenti» — they were his wife's brothers.

src: Arienzo deaths register, 1823 — ANTENATI an_ua14325, 64 images
what: Every act, read for FALCO as deceased, parent, spouse or declarant
got:
No Falco died. But «GIUSEPPE FALCO FU MATTEO» declares twice on 20 June — the first time the CIVIL series states his parentage outright, confirming from a separate series what the parish books said: he is a son of the late Matteo. Also a third, living Maria Falco, wife of Francesco CIOFFI (the archive long read this as Cossi; see Method).

And PAOLO RIVETTI, 50, «figlio del fu Pasquale Rivetti e di Giovanna Perrotta» — the brother of Crescenzo Rivetti, who married Angela Falco. Giovanna Perrotta is named without «fu», so she was still alive in 1823.

src: Arienzo deaths register, 1824 — ANTENATI an_ua14326, 52 images
what: Every act, read for FALCO as deceased, parent, spouse or declarant
got:
No Falco died — but atto 8 has PASQUALE FALCO himself, fifty-five, a COLONO of strada Camellara, declaring beside his brother GIUSEPPE — and the register enters BOTH of them as «ZIO DEL DEFUNTO», uncle, a word this archive transcribed as «vicino» until 16 September 2026. It is the only record in which the ancestor acts rather than being spoken of, and the only one signed in his own hand: «PASCALE FALCO». The dead child's mother is a third, living Maria Falco, and the act calls these two men her brothers — which her stated age forbids, so the word is recorded and the pedigree refused.

Also DONN'ANNA QUOTOLO, eighty-eight, widow of Don Nicola Rivetti — one half of the gentry couple that has been a candidate for Chiara Rivetti's parents since 1816, now with her own act, her age and her father.

src: Arienzo deaths register, 1825 — ANTENATI an_ua14327, 39 images
what: Every act, read for FALCO as deceased, parent, spouse or declarant
got:
MADDALENA FALCO, seven, and CLEMENTE FALCO, fifteen months — Giuseppe Falco and Antonia di Guida buried two children in nineteen days. Maddalena's civil birth act of 7 June 1818 was already in this archive; she died a week short of her seventh birthday.

Giuseppe Falco also declared, for the third time, at a death in the household of Francesco CIOFFI and a third Maria Falco — and the Cossi declared Maddalena's. Two houses standing for each other through five child deaths — and ONE act does say they are kin: the act of 25 March 1824 enters both Falco declarants as «ZIO DEL DEFUNTO». This sentence said «no act ever» until 16 September 2026.

src: Arienzo deaths register, 1826 — ANTENATI an_ua14328, 52 images
what: Every act, read for FALCO as deceased, parent, spouse or declarant
got:
MARIA FALCO, thirty-two, on 25 April — «moglie di ALFONSO DIGLIO … figlia di PASQUALE FALCO … e di CHIARA RIVETTI». A second daughter of generation two, and a sister of Vincenzo. Both parents are named WITHOUT «fu», so Pasquale was alive and still a contadino in 1826 — only the second sighting of him between his marriage and his death.

And on 28 October, GIUSEPPE FALCO, forty-six, massaro, declares an act BESIDE CARLANTONIO MORGILLO, forty-six, of the same street — the first time in the whole series that a Falco and a Morgillo stand together. Eighty-eight acts read; also five Morgillo buried, three religious houses, a gendarme brigadier and the town's royal notary.

src: Arienzo deaths register, 1827 — ANTENATI an_ua14329, 42 images
what: Every act, read for FALCO as deceased, parent, spouse or declarant
got:
No Falco died — but TWO Falco appear. GIUSEPPE FALCO, forty, a COLONO of strada Camellara, declares for the household of Francesco CIOFFI and the third Maria Falco FOR THE FOURTH TIME. And MATTEO FALCO, twenty-eight, a POSSIDENTE of strada Porta di Sopra: the only propertied Falco in twenty registers, bearing the founding ancestor's name, and unjoined.

The volume also holds a MURDER — the Giudicato Regio's own letter, sewn in, about a body found buried in a wood and identified as Mariantonia d'Addio, wife of Pellegrino Morgillo. And Suor Maria Teresa Cossi, dead at ONE HUNDRED AND SEVEN, born 20 January 1720; the register's arithmetic checks.

src: Arienzo deaths register, 1828 — ANTENATI an_ua14330, 48 images
what: Every act, read for FALCO as deceased, parent, spouse or declarant
got:
No Falco died — but atto 54 gives this archive a word it had been waiting for. GIUSEPPE FALCO, fifty-six, of strada Camellara, declares the death of the FIFTH child of Francesco Cioffi and the third Maria Falco, and the register enters him as «PARENTE DELLA DEFUNTA» — kinsman, not neighbour. CORRECTED 16 September 2026: this was published as «the word it had waited six years for» and it was not the first. The act of 25 March 1824 says «ZIO», four years earlier and stronger, and this archive had misread it.

The volume also builds the MORGILLO into households for the first time: Angelo Morgillo, seventy, a colono of Monticello de' Cappuccini, with his sons Nicola and Vincenzo; and Biagio Morgillo of San Gaetano with his brothers Antonio, Simone and Domenico. Seventy acts read.

src: Arienzo deaths register, 1837 — ANTENATI an_ua14339, 78 images
what: Every act, read for FALCO as deceased, parent, spouse or declarant
got:
THE FIND IS NOT A FALCO. Atto 95, 11 September: «sono comparsi ORAZIO MORGILLO, di anni QUARANTADUE, di professione COLONO … strada NUOVA DI SAN GAETANO». This is GENERATION FOUR'S FATHER-IN-LAW — the father of Angela Rosa Morgillo, who married Raffaele Falco — and it is the FIRST RECORD OF HIM this archive has ever had. He was carried on the family tree with no date, no place and no trade; he now has all three, born about 1795, a colono, and living on strada NUOVA DI SAN GAETANO among the San Gaetano Morgillo brothers. And atto 61 has MATTEO FALCO (27) and VINCENZO FALCO (44) declaring TOGETHER on strada Camellara — the earliest sighting of the later Matteo, and the first time Vincenzo's stated age has ever agreed with a document: 44 in 1837 implies 1793, and his marriage act implies the same year.

COMPLETE — images 2 to 78, all 129 acts, ELEVEN duplicate openings, and the arithmetic checks exactly. Reading the whole volume answered a question no partial sweep could: 1837 is the year cholera reached the Kingdom, and the month-by-month count shows a baseline of SEVEN TO TEN deaths a month for nine months — and then TWENTY-THREE in July, with August at fourteen. Two and a half times normal, confined to one month, unlike anything in 1838 or 1839. The register names no causes, so no diagnosis is offered; the count is the finding. Also: GIOVANNA PERROTTA, «d'anni CENTO TRE», born about 1734, the oldest person in the sweeps; the Capuchin convent proved, with three of its men including the house's LETTORE; the Cillo sisters joined across two volumes; a MAIONE living on strada Camellara; GIUSEPPE MAJONE, a second son of Bartolomeo Majone; three generations of di Lucia masons, the last of them twenty-two; and TWICE I read a woman as «MARIA CARFORA» — the name this archive most wants — and twice at 3400 px she was somebody else.

src: Arienzo deaths register, 1838 — ANTENATI an_ua14340, 53 images
what: Every act, read for FALCO as deceased, parent, spouse or declarant
got:
FOUR Falco, three of them on strada Camellara, and a Falco household the archive did not have. Atto 19: «MATTEO FALCO, di anni VENTOTTO, di professione COLONO … strada CAMELLARA» — born about 1810, almost certainly the later Matteo who married Alessandra Crisci, and THE FIRST RECORD OF HIS OWN this archive has ever had for him. Atto 56: GIUSEPPE FALCO, fifty, colono, still standing for the household of Francesco Cioffi ten years after the register called him «parente». Atto 60: VINCENZO FALCO, forty-seven, contadino. And atto 71 buries PASQUALE FALCO, thirteen, «figlio di FRANCESCO FALCO … e di GASPARDA FALCO» — parents new to this archive, both alive.

COMPLETE — images 2 to 53, all 91 acts, five duplicate openings, and the same 1849 ministerial certificate that closes 1840–1843 with its counts left blank. This volume settles the age question: VINCENZO FALCO is forty-seven here and thirty-seven fourteen months later; ANDREA CIOFFI of Camellara is seventy here and buried at eighty-two six months later; GAETANO CIOFFI is fifty-six here and dead at seventy thirteen months later. Also: ANGELO MORGILLO, ninety, «vedovo di MARIA RIVETTI», pushing the Morgillo back to a Gennaro of about 1720 and marrying the line's two flanking surnames to each other; SEVEN Maione households in one year; a Carfora household on Camellara itself burying two children; MARIA ELISABETTA BAUMGARTEN, a Neapolitan officer's daughter working as a spinner; a man dead in an osteria, «nato in Melizzano»; and a woman I first read as «MARIA CARFORA» who turned out at 3400 px to be MARIA CARBONE, widow of a Carfora — the most useful mistake in the volume.

src: Arienzo deaths register, 1839 — ANTENATI an_ua14341, 69 images
what: Every act, read for FALCO as deceased, parent, spouse or declarant
got:
FOUR Falco sightings — and for the first time the two men stand in the town hall TOGETHER. Atto 102, 26 November: «sono comparsi GIUSEPPE FALCO, di anni CINQUANTATRÉ, di professione COLONO … strada CAMELLARA, e VINCENZO FALCO, di anni TRENTASETTE, di professione CONTADINO … strada CAMELLARA». And atto 81 buries FILOMENA FALCO, one year old, «figlia di VINCENZO FALCO … e di ANDRIANA CIOFFI» — a new child of generation three, and a mother's surname that CONTRADICTS the Andreana Crisci this archive publishes. Both readings are left standing.

COMPLETE — images 2 to 69, all 110 acts, seven duplicate openings. The volume swaps the two Falco trades inside one year — Vincenzo is a colono in March and a contadino in November, Giuseppe the reverse — and makes Vincenzo forty-two in March and thirty-seven in November. Also here: DON GIOVANBATTISTA RIVETTI the APOTHECARY, dead at fifty-five, naming his own father; DON FRANCESCO MORGILLO, gentleman, son of a doctor, in the volume's last act; TWO MAIONE households, one of them reaching back to a Bartolomeo Majone of about 1740; a whole CARFORA kindred on strada Signorella; and the hospital pair whose stated ages move by twenty years in sixteen months.

src: Arienzo deaths register, 1840 — ANTENATI an_ua14342, 54 images
what: Every act, read for FALCO as deceased, parent, spouse or declarant
got:
No Falco died, and no Falco declares — but atto 50 gives the EARLIEST of three acts naming RAFFAELE CIOFFI and FRANCESCA FALCO, who buried MADDALENA at one year old on 17 August 1840. With the 1842 and 1843 acts the household is now complete: three children in four years, and the 1843 file's «Domenica Falco» corrected by two independent readings rather than one.

COMPLETE — images 2 to 54, all 87 acts, eight duplicate openings. Also here: MARIA GIUSEPPA SCARPATI, «sorora del Conservatorio di San Filippo», almost certainly the ARCHPRIEST'S SISTER, and with her a SECOND religious house in Arienzo; the household of GIOVANNI CIOFFI, the man who reported Chiara Rivetti's death, with his wife MARIA PORRINO on strada Camellara; a man dead IN THE STREET; a judge of the Vicaria of Naples; and one household — Pasquale Cioffi's — that this volume takes apart child by child and then wife.

src: Arienzo deaths register, 1841 — ANTENATI an_ua14343, 55 images
what: Every act, read for FALCO as deceased, parent, spouse or declarant
got:
THREE Falco sightings, one of them a name the archive had never seen. GIUSEPPE FALCO, colono of strada CAMELLARA, declares twice in October — «di anni cinquantasei» on the 16th and «di anni cinquantatré» on the 19th, three days later, in the same hand. And atto 1, the first act of the year: «e BENEDETTO FALCO, di anni quaranta, contadino, domiciliato in strada CAMELLARA» — born about 1801, recorded and deliberately NOT placed in the line, because no act names his parents.

COMPLETE — images 2 to 55, all 91 acts, nine duplicate openings. Also here: SUOR ARCANGELA, a nun of NINETY-NINE born in Lauro; ANTONIA LOPA, eighty-seven, «nata in FORCHIA», a third member of a Forchia family who moved to Arienzo; a Morgillo living on strada Camellara; and five households that can now be followed across 1841, 1842 and 1843 — including LUCA ZIMBARDO and MARIA MORGILLO, who buried two sons, both named Antonio, a year apart.

src: Arienzo deaths register, 1842 — ANTENATI an_ua14344, 56 images
what: Every act, read for FALCO as deceased, parent, spouse or declarant
got:
TWO Falco sightings and a Falco household the archive did not have. Atto 41, 20 July: «e GIUSEPPE FALCO, di anni CINQUANTADUE, di professione COLONO, domiciliato in strada CAMELLARA». Atto 55, 24 August: «MATTEO FALCO d'anni due, figlio di MICHELE FALCO, contadino, e di ANTONIA MIGLIORE» — a two-year-old dead on the line's own street, and parents both alive. And atto 2 corrects the 1843 file: Raffaele Cioffi's wife is FRANCESCA Falco, not Domenica.

COMPLETE — images 2 to 56, all 86 acts, eleven duplicate openings. Also here: DON ANGELO SCARPATI, the ARCIPRETE of Arienzo, dead at seventy-six in February; DON TOMASO CIOFFI, a priest, in May; eleven Morgillo across seven households, none of them reaching Angela Rosa Morgillo; ORSOLA DIGLIO and her nine-year-old daughter GRAZIA RIVETTI dead on the same day on strada Camellara; and two strangers — a dealer from Magliano and a beggar from Naples — whose parent fields the clerk left BLANK.

src: Arienzo deaths register, 1843 — ANTENATI an_ua14345, 44 images
what: Every act, read for FALCO as deceased, parent, spouse or declarant
got:
CHIARA RIVETTI, wife of Pasquale Falco and generation two of this line — «vedova di PASQUALE FALCO, di anni OTTANTA, contadina, figlia di NICOLA RIVETTI defunto, DI PROFESSIONE CONTADINO, e di ANNA DI RUGGIO defunta», 3 September. The oldest open question in the archive, closed: her father was a labourer, not a Don, and the gentry couple is ruled out.

COMPLETE — images 3 to 44, all 67 acts. Also here: GIUSEPPE FALCO declaring twice, aged fifty-six in May and fifty-five in August, which ends the age question; a FRANCESCA FALCO of the founding generation, married to Gioacchino Cioffi; GENNARO MORGILLO, a colono of STRADA CAMELLARA, whose death Giuseppe Falco declared; and a MORGILLO brother and sister nine days apart — Francesca and Nicola, both children of Gaetano Morgillo and Maria Cioffi, a third Morgillo household with no established tie to the Falco. The volume also holds two nuns of the Ave Grazia Piena, a hundred-year-old basket maker, and an 1849 ministerial certificate recording that six BLANK sheets were cut from it.

src: Arienzo births register, 1816 — ANTENATI an_ua14413, 66 images
what: Every act, read for FALCO as deceased, parent, spouse or declarant
got:
Raffaele Falco, 25 April, son of Vincenzo Falco and Andreana Crisci. Domenico Falco, 25 November, son of a DIFFERENT Giuseppe Falco and Gelsomina Vigliotta, of strada Costa.

The 1816 Raffaele unsettled generation four for a time; the 1817 death register has since closed it. The register ran to 123 acts; all 122 fathers read are logged.

what: Every act, read for FALCO as deceased, parent, spouse or declarant

Raffaele Falco, 10 May, son of Vincenzo and Andreana — generation four. Maddalena Falco, 7 June, daughter of Giuseppe Falco and Antonia di Guida, of strada Camellara.

src: ANTENATI an_ua14258 (43 images) and an_ua14260 (57 images), «atti di solenne promessa di matrimonio». 1856 carries a FILLED alphabetical index bound at the FRONT, on image 3; 1854 does not.
what: The Arienzo marriage registers of 1854 and 1856
got: TWO FALCO FOUND AND THE ONE SOUGHT ABSENT. GIUSEPPE FALCO of strada Costa remarried on 13 December 1854 to Angela Carfora — the act names his parents for the first time and gives him as VEDOVO DI GELSOMINA VIGLIOTTI, living at SANTA MARIA A VICO. PASQUA FALCO married ANGELO MAJONE on 9 September 1856, atto 29 — thirty-three, daughter of Giuseppe Falco and the late Gelsomina Vigliotta, and NOT described as a widow, which proves she is NOT the Pasqua Falco who married Francesco Arricale and bore generation five’s wife in 1848. NUNZIATA FALCO IS IN NEITHER YEAR, and not in 1855 either — all three volumes read act by act. She is held here as marrying 13 [Nov] 1855 with the month in brackets. Either that date is wrong or she married at her husband’s comune.

src: ANTENATI an_ua14259, all 28 «atti di solenne promessa di matrimonio», images 2–30 — swept three times, once for the groom, once for his parents, once for the bride.
what: The Arienzo marriage register of 1855, read act by act
got: ONE FALCO BRIDE AND NOT THE ONE EXPECTED. SARA FALCO, atto 6, 14 February 1855, to ANTONIO MAURO, fruttajolo of strada Croce — the daughter found three days ago in the 1828 tavola, now proved to have lived to twenty-six. But NUNZIATA FALCO, her sister, held here as marrying 13 [Nov] 1855 with the month in brackets, IS NOT IN THIS VOLUME. Two daughters of one house marrying in one year and the civil register carries only one. Either the parish date is wrong, or she married at her husband’s comune — which would invert the rule this archive has proved twice, that a couple marries in the BRIDE’s parish. THE FINDING AID AFTER 1849: the «Matrimoni, indice» series stops at 1849, but the REGISTERS run on at `an_ua14213` + (year − 1809), 28–37 acts a year, each naming both spouses, both sets of parents, and the parish celebration date in the margin. The register is the index.

src: ANTENATI «Morti, indice» — thirteen annual volumes, 55 images, every page’s surname column cropped and tiled so the whole stretch could be scanned for one name. 1836 does not exist in the series.
what: The Arienzo death indexes, 1831–1843
got: TWO NEW CHILDREN AND FIVE EMPTY YEARS. New: PASQUALE FALCO, 30 October 1838, a fourth child of the first-cousin marriage of Francescantonio Falco and Raffaela Falco; and MATTEO FALCO, 24 August 1842, a third child of Michelangelo Falco and Mariantonia Vigliotta. ALREADY HELD, and checked before being claimed: Anna Falco 1831, Giovanna and Carmina Falco 1832, Pasquale Falco 1833. NO FALCO AT ALL in 1835, 1837, 1839, 1840 or 1843. ONE YEAR IS NOT A NEGATIVE: the 1834 index is a SINGLE LEAF covering A to C and marked END, so any Falco who died that year is invisible in it — only the register itself will show them. One candidate was rejected at magnification: a row that read FALCO on the tile is CRISCI in the hand.

src: ANTENATI «Morti, indice», an_ua14271 + (year − 1809) — seven consecutive years, each line giving the dead person, town, trade, BOTH PARENTS and the date.
what: The Arienzo death indexes, 1824–1830
got: GIUSEPPE NUNZIO FALCO, born 25 March 1824 to Vincenzo Falco and Andreana Crisci, IS IN NONE OF THEM — the whole of his early childhood. The only Falco deaths in the seven years are ones this archive already holds: MADDALENA and CLEMENTE in 1825, MARIA FALCO (wife of Alfonso Diglio) in 1826, and ROSA FALCO, daughter of the founders and wife of Carlantonio Morgillo, on 16 October 1830. 1824, 1827, 1828 and 1829 have NO F SECTION AT ALL. A child who is born and never dies in his own parish is the ordinary shape of a man who lived, so the burden is now on finding him alive — the next places are the marriage indexes after 1849 and the death registers from 1831. ARITHMETIC WARNING: this series slips exactly as the marriage indexes do — 1836 is MISSING, and from `an_ua14298` the labels run a year ahead.

src: ANTENATI an_ua14413 (1816, 62 acts) and an_ua14414 (1817, 109 acts) — every opening swept at the declarant line, both half-pages, since this form carries a whole act on each half.
what: The Arienzo birth registers of 1816 and 1817, read act by act
got: THE ELDER GIOVANNI FALCO IS IN NEITHER. He was buried 27 November 1841 «annorum 24 circiter», which points at these two years, and 1817 holds NOT ONE FALCO BIRTH from any of the four Falco houses at Arienzo, while 1816 holds exactly one — Domenico Falco, 25 November, to GIUSEPPE FALCO of STRADA COSTA and Gelsomina Vigliotta, which this archive already had. So either his stated age is wrong, or he was born in a year not yet read (1815, or 1818–1820), or his birth is only in the PARISH register. WARNING FOR ANYONE FOLLOWING: the printed year on these forms is unreliable. `an_ua14414` reads «sedici» in print on every page and IS 1817 — the clerk struck the printed word and wrote «diciassette» above it by hand. `an_ua14415` is printed «sedici» and is 1818.

src: ANTENATI an_ua14416, 74 images. THE YEAR IS CONFIRMED FROM THE MANUSCRIPT, not the label: the title page reads «Dal primo Gennajo a tutto il dì trentuno Dicembre mille ottocento DICIANNOVE» and the last acts are dated December 1819. 137 acts.
what: The Arienzo birth register of 1819, read act by act
got: THIS VOLUME HAS NO ANNUAL TAVOLA. Both ends were checked, which is this archive's rule after 1859 and 1860 disagreed about where an index sits. The last leaf carries a TWENTY-ONE ROW list of parents and birth dates under «Nomi, e cognomi de' genitori | Giorno della nascita | Osservazioni» — Rivetti, Arrigale, Laudato, Morgillo, Pesciutelli, Cossi, di Lucia, Cioffi, Martone, d'Ambrosio, Lizzarulo, delle Cave, Lettieri, Sposito, Balletta, della Morte, Sapano. NO FALCO IN IT, and it is NOT the year's index: twenty-one rows against 137 acts. So the year was read act by act, in six contact sheets of twenty-four bands. THREE FALCO BIRTHS, ALL ON STRADA CAMELLARA: act 33, 18 March, DOMENICO CLEMENTE, of Giuseppe Falco massaro di campagna and Gelsomina Vigliotta; act 99, 11 October, CRESCENZO, of Giuseppe Falco contadino and Antonia di Guida; act 133, 21 December, LUIGI, of Vincenzo Falco and Andreana Crisci. AND A NEGATIVE THAT MATTERS: ROSARIA FALCO, who died 15 March 1819 as a daughter of Giuseppe Falco and Gelsomina Vigliotta, IS NOT IN THIS VOLUME EITHER. She was already absent from 1816, 1817 and 1818. Her birth act has now been looked for in every year it could be in, and it is in none of them.

src: ANTENATI an_ua14367, 86 images, 147 acts. YEAR CONFIRMED FROM THE MANUSCRIPT title page: «Dal primo Gennajo a tutto il dì trentuno Dicembre mille ottocento sessantacinque». NO TAVOLA AT EITHER END — both checked — so it was read act by act in seven contact sheets at the band where the deceased's name sits.
what: The Arienzo DEATH register of 1865 — the last volume in the series
got: NOT ONE FALCO DEATH IN THE YEAR. This is the LAST Arienzo death volume Antenati holds, and it matters because VINCENZO FALCO, generation three, is demonstrably ALIVE on 16 December 1864 — named without «fu» in his son Luigi's death act, a colono still on strada Camellara at seventy-two, in a register that marks four other dead parents on the same opening. SO HIS DEATH IS 1866 OR LATER, in the post-Unification Stato civile italiano this archive has never located for Arienzo. The same now holds for GIUSEPPE FALCO of Antonia di Guida, alive November 1849 and in no volume since. WHAT 1865 DOES HOLD: «e MATTEO FALCO di anni cinquantanove» as a DECLARANT in December — the second Matteo Falco, alive at about fifty-nine; and ANGELO MAJONE, 56, declaring in October — Pasqua Falco's first husband alive nine years after their wedding. A NAMESAKE CAUTION: act at image 68 buries a MARIA CARFORA at Arienzo on 24 October 1865. She is NOT generation seven's grandmother, who is of Forchia and bore children from 1883. This archive has twice been caught reading a woman as «Maria Carfora» because it wanted her to be.

src: ANTENATI an_ua14213 + (year − 1809), running to 1865 = an_ua14269. THE «MATRIMONI, INDICE» SERIES STOPS AT 1849, so after that the register IS the index — each act naming both spouses, BOTH SETS OF PARENTS, ages, trades, streets, which parents were dead, and the church date facing it. A FIRST ATTEMPT DECLARED THIS SERIES TO END IN 1858; that was four fetches refused by a rate-limiting host and read as absences, and it is withdrawn on the corrections page.
what: The Arienzo MARRIAGE REGISTERS after the index series ends — FINISHED, 1850 to 1865
got: SIXTEEN YEARS READ ACT BY ACT. TWO FALCO MARRIAGES IN ALL OF THEM. 1850 (11 acts): ACT 6 IS MICHELE FALCO, 43, colono of strada Camellara, VEDOVO DI ANTONIA VIGLIOTI, marrying GIOVANNA D'AMBROGIO, 19 — one word merging two households this archive had kept apart, and naming his parents RAFFAELE FALCO and CHIARA RIVETTI, both dead. 1861 (29 acts): ACT 16 IS STANISLAO FALCO, 24, PASTORE, son of VINCENZO FALCO and ANDREANA CRISCI — A CHILD OF GENERATION THREE THIS ARCHIVE DID NOT HAVE — marrying FILOMENA DI LUCIA, 23, daughter of the late Luigi di Lucia and Marta di Nizzo; church 23 September at Sant'Andrea Apostolo, and BOTH HIS PARENTS UNMARKED BY «FU» while the bride's father is marked in the next clause. NIL YEARS: 1851 (24 acts), 1852 (two bound registers, ~9 then 30), 1853 (29), 1857 (32), 1858 (36), 1859 (25), 1860 (34), 1862 (27), 1863 (21), 1864 (~25), 1865 (~36). 1854, 1855 and 1856 were read earlier and gave three Falco weddings. AND A FIND THAT IS NOT A FALCO AT ALL: 1860 act 3, 20 January, is SABBATINO ANNECCHINO of FORCHIA — son of fu CARMINE ANNECCHINO and fu ROSA CEGLIA — marrying MARIA ANTONIA CARFORA, NATA IN ARIENZO, daughter of fu [?]erio CARFORA and fu PASQUA MORGILLO. THE CARFORA ARE AN ARIENZO FAMILY, which every previous route to them assumed they were not. ALSO: the 1861 volume binds a NOTIFICAZIONI register after its acts — banns, with both sets of parents in a cleaner hand, published where a couple LIVES even when the wedding is celebrated elsewhere.

src: ANTENATI «Matrimoni, indice», 40 volumes covering 1809–1849 with 1836 MISSING. 116 images in all. Arithmetic: an_ua14108 + (year − 1809) to 1835, then 14107 + (year − 1809) from 1837.
what: The Arienzo marriage indexes — what is read and what is not
got: FINISHED. Every year from 1809 to 1849 has been read — 116 images, each checked against ITS OWN TAVOLA HEADING rather than the catalogue label, and each carried to the closing certificate where the register states the year’s total. 1836 does not exist in the series. THIRTEEN FALCO MARRIAGES were found and all are published, with five more Falco reached through the parents’ column. NO FALCO MARRIED AT ARIENZO in 1809, 1810, 1811, 1812, 1815 (bar Luigi of the Sebastiano house), 1816, 1817, 1820, 1821, 1822, 1823, 1824, 1826, 1827, 1830, 1831, 1833, 1835, 1837, 1838, 1841, 1843, 1844 or 1849. THE ONE RECORD THIS SWEEP SET OUT TO FIND AND DID NOT: the marriage of MARIA FALCO to FRANCESCO CIOFFI (this entry read COSSI until 15 September; the surname is CIOFFI, corrected from the 1825 register at full resolution, and the sweep was run on the BRIDE so the reading is unaffected). Their son died in March 1824 aged five, so it is no later than about 1819, and 1809–1819 is now read out entirely. The likely answer is that THE ARIENZO CIVIL REGISTERS BEGIN IN 1809 and this marriage is older than they are — which would require her stated age of twenty-five in 1824 to be wrong by roughly eight years, a margin this register reaches routinely. The next instrument is the PARISH marriage register, not another index.

src: ANTENATI «Matrimoni, indice» for 1837, 1838, 1839, 1840–1849 — the F section of every year read, and every page of the years that yielded a Falco. 1836 IS MISSING from the series and the last index is 1849.
what: The Arienzo marriage indexes, 1837–1849
got: FIVE FALCO MARRIAGES IN THE THIRTEEN YEARS, all five published: FRANCESCA MARIA LUCIA FALCO to Raffaele Crisci, 5 January 1839 — which closed the two-daughters question; CRESCENZO FALCO to Angela Maria Morgillo, 3 February 1845, closing a window the archive could only date «c. 1831–46»; ANDREA FALCO to MARIA CARMELA BUONO, 24 May 1846, which supplied her surname for the first time; ANGELANDREA FALCO to Maria Cimmino, March 1847; and FRANCESCO FALCO OF AIROLA to Giuseppa Rivetti, 23 August 1848 — a different house, no kinship claimed. NO FALCO MARRIED IN 1837, 1838, 1841, 1843, 1844 OR 1849. The Falco who appear as PARENTS rather than spouses are the Lettieri of Paolisi, whose mother Giovanna Falco married two children off at Arienzo in 1826 and 1837 and is STILL attached to no Falco household.

src: ANTENATI «Matrimoni, indice» for 1828, 1829, 1830, 1831, 1832, 1833, 1834 and 1835, read line by line. 1836 IS MISSING from the series entirely.
what: The Arienzo marriage indexes, 1828–1835
got: FOUR FALCO MARRIAGES IN THE EIGHT YEARS, all four now published: MICHELANGELO FALCO (of Pasquale and Chiara Rivetti) to Antonia Vigliotti, December 1828; GIOVANNA FALCO (of Giuseppe and Antonia di Guida) to Aniello Crisci, 6 September 1829; FRANCESCANTONIO FALCO (of Pasquale) to RAFFAELA FALCO (of Giuseppe) — first cousins — 16 July 1832; and MATTEO FALCO (of Giuseppe) to Alessandra Crisci, 24 January 1834. NO FALCO MARRIED IN 1830, 1831, 1833 OR 1835. Three of the four brides or grooms were CRISCI, the family next door on strada Camellara, and the fourth was a Falco. FRANCESCA MARIA LUCIA FALCO, born 1812, is in NONE of these years — she remains the open half of the two-daughters question, and 1837–1849 have not yet been read.

src: ANTENATI «Matrimoni, indice» — 1825 an_ua14124 (25 marriages), 1826 an_ua14125 (17, a whole year on one page), 1827 an_ua14126 (20). Read line by line.
what: The Arienzo marriage indexes, 1825–1827
got: NO FALCO MARRIED IN ANY OF THE THREE. What the three years gave instead, all of it through the PARENTS column: LUCIA RIVETTI, a fourth child of Angela Falco, married 7 February 1825; a GIOVANNA FALCO at PAOLISI whose son Ludovico Lettieri married 2 February 1826, too old to be either Giovanna this archive holds; and ALFONSO DIGLIO marrying again on 2 April 1827, which is what dated the death of his first wife MARIA FALCO and led to the act that finally named her parents. ARITHMETIC WARNING: the series is `an_ua14108` + (year − 1809) only up to 1835. From 1837 it is `14107` + (year − 1809); 1836 is MISSING from the series; `an_ua14148` has no manifest; and the last index is 1849. The death indexes slip the same way after 1834.

src: ANTENATI «Matrimoni, indice», an_ua14108 + (year − 1809) — one to four images a year, each line giving the act number, both spouses, each one’s patria, BOTH sets of parents and the date of the church wedding.
what: The Arienzo marriage indexes, 1818 and 1821–1824
got: NO FALCO MARRIED IN 1821 (16 marriages), 1822 (22), 1823 (26) OR 1824 (25) — read line by line, and the Falco who appear do so only as PARENTS of a spouse. What the four years did give: ANNA FALCO’s own wedding, 3 May 1818, with her husband’s parents named; and two sons of Angela Falco and Crescenzo Rivetti marrying, GIOVANNI on 23 December 1821 and PASQUALE on 29 July 1824. CAUTION FOR ANYONE FOLLOWING: the sort order is not stable — 1818 is by FORENAME, 1821–1824 by SURNAME — and the 1824 tavola holds TWO grooms called Pasquale Rivetti, first cousins, told apart only by the parents’ column. 1812–1817, 1819–1820 and 1825 onward are NOT yet read.

src: ANTENATI an_ua14421, images 2–153 — the year's tavola is covered by an inserted leaf in the filming, the same obstruction as 1825, so every opening was rendered and the declarant, the mother and the father read on each one. Closed 31 December 1824 by Giovan Battista de Baptistis, secondo eletto.
what: The Arienzo birth register of 1824, read end to end
got: THREE FALCO ACTS IN THE YEAR, and all three are now published. Atto 26, CLEMENTE FALCO, 11 March, to Giuseppe Falco and Antonia di Guida of strada Camellara — the birth act of a child held until now only by his death at fifteen months. Atto 31, GIUSEPPE NUNZIO FALCO, 25 March, to Vincenzo Falco and Andreana Crisci — a NEW son. Atto 73, GIUSEPPA CIOFFI, 18 June, to Francesco Cioffi and the MARIA FALCO who was twenty-five — again a child held only by her death. Nothing else. NO PASQUA FALCO. Three Arricale appear (Agostino 36, Marcello 30, and a Raffaela who is a mother) and are recorded elsewhere. The `Foglio` surname runs right through this volume and this scribe's Foglio and Falco are nearly the same word; every candidate was magnified before it was accepted or dropped.

src: ANTENATI an_ua14343, all ninety acts, images 8–54 — swept at the band carrying the deceased's name and age, then the November acts rendered whole.
what: The Arienzo death register of 1841, read end to end
got: NOT ONE FALCO IN THE YEAR. This was read to find the civil act behind a parish burial of 27 November 1841 — «Joannes Falco filius Josephi et Antoniae di Guida, aetatis suae annorum 24 circiter» — and there is none. The register goes from act 86, a child buried 26 November, to act 87, a tailor of eighty buried 7 December; the days on either side are accounted for. Arienzo's civil and parish registers normally agree, so a burial with no civil act is itself evidence: it is now more likely that the 1841 transcript is wrong, or belongs to another parish in the same filmed set, than that Giuseppe Falco and Antonia di Guida really had two living sons named Giovanni. The image behind the transcript has still not been read.

src: ANTENATI an_ua14422, all 134 acts on 133 folios, images 2–141 — the year's alphabetical tavola is unusable, so every opening was rendered and the declarant, the mother and the father read on each one.
what: The Arienzo birth register of 1825, read end to end
got: EXACTLY TWO FALCO ACTS IN THE YEAR. Atto 42, GIOVANNI, son of Giuseppe Falco and Antonia di Guida of strada Camellara, born 6 April — which turned out to be the civil birth act of DON GIOVANNI FALCO the deacon, already held from his parish baptism. And atto 72, CLEMENTINA DIGLIO, born 30 May to Alfonso Diglio and a fourth MARIA FALCO. Nothing else. NO PASQUA FALCO, and no child for Pasquale Falco and Chiara Rivetti, for Vincenzo Falco and Andreana Crisci, or for any other Falco house. Three Arricale appear — Giuseppe (29), Raffaele (27, on strada Capodiconca) and Pellegrina — and are recorded on the Arricale sheet rather than here. The `Foglio` surname occurs repeatedly in this volume and this scribe renders it almost identically to `Falco`; every candidate was magnified to the word before it was accepted or dropped.

src: ANTENATI an_ua14422, images 142–144, the back of the volume.
what: The 1825 alphabetical tavola — filmed, but not readable here
got: OBSTRUCTED, AND NOT WORTH A SECOND ATTEMPT FROM THIS COPY. The closing certificate is there — «*abbiamo chiuso e firmato il presente registro degl'atti di Nascita, di fogli scritti num. centotrentatré, contenente atti num. CENTOTRENTAQUATTRO*», signed 31 December 1825 by Giovanbattista Rivetti — but the tavola leaf facing it is COVERED BY AN INSERTED SHEET in the filming, and the photographer's own card lies across the foot of the frame reading «THIS INDEX HAS BEEN MICROFILMED ALREADY». So the index exists and was shot in another filming. Until that filming is found, 1825 can only be read act by act, which is what was done. The same obstruction pattern already blocks 1821 and 1824.

src: ANTENATI an_ua14425, the Tavola Alfabetica Annuale at images 127–128, read for every letter.
what: The Arienzo birth register of 1828, through its tavola
got: ONE FALCO BIRTH IN THE YEAR, AND ONLY ONE: atto 118, SARA FALCO, 19 December, daughter of Vincenzo Falco and Andreana Crisci — published today. The F group holds three entries in act-number order, 43 Ferro, 82 Ferriello and 118 Falco, and THE GROUP RUNS ACROSS A PAGE BREAK. A working note here said «1828 holds no Falco» on the strength of the first page alone, and it was wrong. No Pasqua Falco, and no child for Giuseppe Falco and Antonia di Guida in 1828.

src: FindMyPast, on subscription, September 2026 — every family surname searched with name variants on, worldwide and filtered to Australia & New Zealand.
what: The Zampiello and the Annecchino, in FindMyPast
got: Nothing. ZAMPIELLO returns two Australian hits and both are United States war records the region filter has mis-tagged; of 81 Zampiello travel and migration records worldwide, every single one goes to the United States, not one to Australia. ANNECCHINO returns zero in Australia and New Zealand. RAFFAELE FALCO returns zero. The family that reached Brisbane is simply not in this archive — which closes the search rather than opening it.

src: FindMyPast: all 56 Australian birth, marriage and death records for Falco, and all 31 electoral-roll entries, read individually.
what: The Queensland Falco — a different family
got: Every Queensland Falco IN FINDMYPAST belongs to one household in the Burdekin cane country, about 1,200 km north of Brisbane: Giuseppe Falco, born about 1898, who married Mary Rubiolo in 1932 and was buried at Home Hill in 1979, with Bartolomeo, Maria Margherita, Primo, Raymond and Laurence at Ayr. This matters for one of our open questions: the Giuseppe Falco who reached Brisbane on the Palermo in 1925 is NOT this man, and remains untraced. CORRECTED SEPTEMBER 2026: this entry used to say «every Queensland Falco», without the qualifier, and that was wrong. Queensland's own index holds four members of Carminantonio's Brisbane household — see the sweep below. The Burdekin finding stands; it was never the whole of Queensland, only the whole of FindMyPast.

src: familyhistory.bdm.qld.gov.au, September 2026 — fifty-four surnames from this archive and its neighbours, exact-match, across all three registers. The index covers births to 1926, marriages to 1951 and deaths to 1996, so anyone who died after 1996 cannot appear whatever the truth is.
what: The Queensland historical index, swept surname by surname
got: Four of this family found, and they are on the register page with their registration numbers. Nothing at all for ANNECCHINO, ZAMPIELLO, SERVODIO, QUOTOLO, MORGILLO, SCHETTINI, CIOFFI, FALCONE, COSSI, MARTONE or CIMMINO. The ZAMPIELLO null is expected rather than troubling: all four Zampiello women who reached Brisbane died in 2004 or later, outside the thirty-year window, so the index could not hold them. The ANNECCHINO null is the harder one — Filomena is in it only under her married name, and her father Carmine is named on her death entry but has no entry of his own.

src: FindMyPast — Italy Births & Baptisms 1806-1900, Italy Deaths & Burials 1809-1900, Italy Marriages 1809-1900.
what: Anything new in FindMyPast's Italian records
got: Nothing new. Every transcript carries the line «Index (c) IRI. Used by permission of FamilySearch Intl» — these are the FamilySearch index this archive harvested directly long ago, re-hosted. There is no second Italian source here.

src: 1,145 pages of the Arienzo parish death register, harvested from FamilySearch's full text and searched by name, by OCR variant, and by male-adult-with-age across 1828–1845.
what: Pasquale Falco's death, in the parish registers
got: It is not there. It was found only in the civil register, by reading 1834 act by act.

src: All 1,162 Falco records in FamilySearch's index of Caserta civil registration 1809–1866, of which 249 fall in the window.
what: Pasquale Falco, in the FamilySearch index
got: The only «Pasquale Falco» principals are two Falcone men of other families.

src: The Arienzo birth registers for 1816, 1817 and 1818, all read act by act.
what: Maria Rosa Falco's birth
got: Absent from all three. She was sixteen at her death in May 1834. Either the age was loose by more than two years, she was born outside Arienzo, or she was baptised without a civil act. Michele Falco of strada Camellara therefore remains undated.

src: 2,056 transcribed pages of the Arienzo marriage and death registers, searched for a marriage to Francesca Crisci between about 1760 and 1766.
what: Matteo Falco's marriage
got: Not found. It would name his father, and it is the line's frontier. His own baptism falls in the gap the register leaves between 1738 and 1761.

src: Antenati — the marriage supplement file for Vincenzo Falco's marriage of 15 October 1814.
what: The Arienzo processetti of 1817
got: FOUND, and the search had been hunting a number that does not exist. The file is in the 1814 volume at BUNDLE 16, images 265-274, and the marriage it supports is ACT 16 of 15 October 1814. This row previously read «the 1814 volume runs to act 25 and stops; act 26's file is in neither volume» — a null built on «act 26 of 15 December 1814», three elements misread off one line of the register in an earlier session. There is no act 26 in the 1814 marriage register: it runs to act 17 and stops. The bundle number and the act number are the same number.

src: Geneanet, 15 September 2026. ANNECCHINO, ZAMPIELLO and ARRICALE searched in full; the site had been cited here only once, in a list of surname-FREQUENCY lookups beside Forebears and Cognomix, which is not a record harvest.
what: Geneanet — its Campania trees, searched at last
got: Almost nothing, and the almost is worth stating. Its Italian record collections are the FamilySearch index re-hosted — the same «Italy, Marriages 1809-1900» that FindMyPast sells — so they hold nothing this archive has not already read from the images. Its USER TREES are the real asset and they do not reach this family: all 499 ANNECCHINO are at FOGGIA, in Puglia, not Forchia. All 29 ZAMPIELLO are a Connecticut and Rhode Island diaspora out of San Martino in Avellino and Monte San Biagio in Latina — a different Zampiello stock, and NONE from Arpaia. There is no Giovanna Arricale at all. THE ONE THING WORTH KEEPING: ARRICALE returns 67, heavily Arienzo, and two member trees — «marcorlando70» and «jimino» — do cover Arienzo people, including MARCELLO GIOVANNI ARRICALE, born 1876 at Arienzo, died 1963 at Altavilla Irpina. That is the first user-submitted tree this archive has found standing on its own ground. It does not touch the line, but anyone extending the Arricale should start there.

src: Three sources this archive will not spend time on, set down so the decision is visible rather than repeated.
what: FreeBMD, RootsChat and Arcanum — not searched, and deliberately
got: FREEBMD indexes the civil registration of ENGLAND AND WALES from 1837. This family has no English generation: it goes Arienzo to Forchia to Arpaia to Brisbane, and the one crossing is Naples to Australia. There is nothing there to find. ROOTSCHAT is a discussion forum, overwhelmingly British and Irish, and a question posted there would be answered by the same FamilySearch and Antenati images this archive reads directly — it is a place to ask, not a source to harvest. ARCANUM digitises the Hungarian and wider Habsburg press and archives; Campania was Bourbon and then Italian, never Habsburg, and no generation of this family lived under Vienna. ALL THREE ARE CLOSED. If that ever changes it will be because a descendant married into one of those countries, which is a different question from this one.

src: The National Archives (UK), Discovery — discovery.nationalarchives.gov.uk, 17 September 2026. The catalogue over TNA's own holdings at Kew plus some 2,500 other British archives. Every surname in this archive searched.
what: Falco, Zampiello, Annecchino, Arricale, Carfora, Crisci, Morgillo, Rivetti — and the three towns, Arienzo, Forchia, Arpaia
got:
**A CLEAN NIL FOR THE FAMILY, AND ONE RECORD ABOUT THE TOWN.**

**ZAMPIELLO 0 · ANNECCHINO 0 · ARRICALE 0 · CARFORA 0 · MORGILLO 0 · RIVETTI 0 · CRISCI 1 · FORCHIA 0 · ARPAIA 0.**

**FALCO returns 86, and not one of them can be this family.** They are British records of people who happened to bear the name: **eighteen WO service records** of British soldiers (service numbers, dates of birth 1903–1925); **twenty-one BT records** of merchant seamen registered at UK ports — «*R360597 FALCO J 11/10/1926 LONDON*», «*R542406 FALCO A 16/08/1917 SANTIAGO, CHILE*»; **twelve HO files**, mostly naturalisation certificates of Italians resident in Britain, the nearest being **Luigi Falco, born 17 July 1894 at SAVIANO**; a company dissolved in 1995; a lawsuit of 1515; and a Lake Como steamer. **«Falco Arienzo» returns 0. «Falco Caserta» returns 0.**

**This family has no British generation, and the catalogue confirms it rather than merely failing to contradict it.** The path is Arienzo → Forchia → Arpaia → Naples → Brisbane, and nobody on it registered as an alien, served the Crown, or signed on at a British port.

**BUT ONE FILE NAMES THE TOWN, AND IT IS WORTH ORDERING.** **WO 32/22147**, 1–31 March 1945: «*Special Investigation Branch investigation: alleged murder of Herron FG, Private, 1583838, Argyle and Sutherland Highlanders **by two Italian civilians at ARIENZO, Italy, 11 March 1945***». Open since 25 August 2017, held at Kew, **not digitised**. A British military police file about a killing in this family's town, five months before the war ended, which would name the accused and its witnesses. **It is a lead about Arienzo, not about the Falco, and it is recorded as that.**

src: Arienzo, «Registro degli atti diversi» — ANTENATI, 45 volumes, `an_ua14064`–`an_ua14106` plus `an_ua57637`–`57638`. The register of births at sea, recognitions, adoptions, PEOPLE WHO DIED AWAY FROM THEIR OWN HOME, and stillbirths. Read end to end, 17–20 September 2026.
what: FALCO and DI GUIDA — and in particular the deaths of ANTONIA DI GUIDA, alive 2 February 1845, and GIUSEPPE FALCO of Antonia di Guida, alive 26 November 1849
got:
**NO FALCO IN ANY OF THE FORTY-FIVE VOLUMES, AND NO DI GUIDA.** Every act from **1845 to 1865** is read and its dead are named — the whole window either person could fall in. Four acts in the series remain unnamed, all **before 1845**, so neither can be among them.

**When an Arienzo person died elsewhere, the comune where they died drew the act and sent a certified copy home, and Arienzo copied it in whole** — age, trade, street, both parents, whether they were dead, surviving children with their ages. So this was the one instrument that could hold a death the town never recorded. **It does not hold theirs.**

**What it does hold is about thirty-five deaths away from home, and they map where an Arienzo labourer went and did not come back from**: the **Ospedale degli Incurabili** at Naples (5), **Sant'Agostino degli Scalzi** at Aversa (3), the **Real Stabilimento de' Matti** and its women's side at Aversa (6), **Acerra** (3), **Caserta** (2), **Airola** (2), a masseria in the **Nola** district, **Montesarchio**, **Santa Maria Maggiore**, the **Ospedale della Trinità** — and once, **LIPARI**.

**PASQUALE PORRINO**, 52, a labourer born at Arienzo, died **31 October 1864 in the hospital of the DOMICILIATI COATTI on Lipari** — internal exile. **CARLO BALLETTA**, soldier of the **1st Dragoons**, died in the Ospedale della Trinità on 3 March 1855, his colonel writing to ask the sindaco to tell his family to collect **one ducat and thirty-five grana**, the price of his kit. **ANGELO IMBIMBO**, 60, died in the Aversa madhouse on 30 November 1855 — and **FRANCESCO IMBIMBO, «figlio d'Angelo»**, died in the **same asylum** on 4 November 1844. **Father and son, eleven years apart.**

**TWO CAUTIONS FOR ANYONE FOLLOWING.** The holdings query `localita=Arienzo` matches **several comuni** — Corpo d'Arienzo, **San Felice d'Arienzo**, **San Casale di Arienzo** — and the printed title page gives the CIRCONDARIO at the top, which is the district, not the town. **Read the comune from each volume's own title page.** And **from 1856 the clerk leaves the printed act heading blank and writes only the body**, so a sweep of the heading band reports «no acts» for a volume holding five.
